name: Dodo
title: Father of one of David's heroes
summary: Dodo is mentioned in the Bible as the father of Eleazar, one of David's three most powerful warriors. He belonged to the Ahohite clan and was from the tribe of Issachar. The name Dodo appears in several places in the Old Testament and may refer to more than one person.

keyEvents.title: Dodo mentioned as father of Eleazar
keyEvents.description: Dodo from the Ahohite clan is identified as the father of Eleazar, one of David's three foremost heroes who distinguished himself in battle.

keyEvents.title: Eleazar's heroic deed at Pas-Dammim
keyEvents.description: Dodo's son Eleazar was with David when the Philistines gathered for battle, and he stood his ground and struck down the Philistines until his hand grew stiff around his sword.

keyEvents.title: Dodo from Issachar as tribal leader
keyEvents.description: A Dodo from the tribe of Issachar is mentioned as the father of the judge Tola, who judged Israel for twenty-three years.

keyEvents.title: Dodo from Bethlehem as the father of Elhanan
keyEvents.description: Another Dodo from Bethlehem is mentioned as the father of Elhanan, who was among David's thirty mighty men.

keyEvents.title: The three mighty men fetching water from the well at Bethlehem
keyEvents.description: In connection with Eleazar, son of Dodo, and the other heroes, three of David's mighty men broke through the Philistine camp to fetch water from the well by the gate of Bethlehem.
